LUMI.TA.plan_name: Bank Option Plan approved 1 June 2022 (filed with ITA 30 June 2022); employee outlines of 16 August 2022 and 12 June 2025 (ref. 2025-01-042103, scribal correction 28 April 2026, ref. 2026-01-039135)
LUMI.TA.strike_rule: Public grants under later outlines: exercise price = average closing price of the Bank share on TASE over the 30 trading days preceding the Board resolution approving the allocation (Outline 12 June 2025 §8.3, as restated in the 11 June 2026 report). For the 10 June 2026 award the exercise price is NIS 72.45. The 16 August 2022 outline used two rules: the August 2022 actual allocation was the official close on the trading day preceding Board approval (NIS 34.3, §8.2); future grants under that same 2022 outline were already to use the 30-trading-day average (§8.3). The 2022 outline also defines a 'Base Price' as the close on the trading day preceding Board approval, used for the ceiling rate (not as the later-grant strike). Individual allocation letters may use a different strike; a private grant letter described to the calculator project (grant 1.6.2026, strike = close before Board approval, default adjusted strike 69.2744) was not matched to a public Maya report in this run and should not be treated as the bank-wide public formula.
LUMI.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: Exercise price (exercise increment) is reduced by the amount of cash dividend distributed, if the record date precedes exercise, including for unvested options (2022 outline §12.5; 11 June 2026 report §3.5, same rule). Floor: exercise increment shall not be less than par value or 30 agorot or another TASE minimum (2022 outline §12.7). Bonus shares, rights issues and capital restructurings have separate proportional adjustments (§12.3-12.6).
LUMI.TA.vesting_schedule: Depends on series and grant. June 2026 award: Series 1 (104,154 options) vests in two equal tranches — 50% two years from allocation, 50% three years from allocation — subject to continued employment in the Bank group and capital-adequacy conditions (total CAR and CET1 not below Banking Supervision minima in the prior calendar year); missed conditions defer vesting by one year at a time until expiry. Series 3 (110,982 options) is performance-linked (annual measurable bonus eligibility) and continued employment; if a portion exceeds a cap relative to fixed compensation, exercise of Series 3 is staggered in three 16.67% steps. The 2022 outline default (unless the Bank determines otherwise) was three equal annual tranches vesting 1, 2 and 3 years from allocation, also subject to capital-adequacy conditions. A private grant letter described to the calculator (vest 1.6.2026 / 1.6.2027 / 1.6.2028, first tranche on grant date) is not the default in the 2022 outline or the June 2026 public award and was not verified in a public report.
LUMI.TA.expiry_term: June 2026 Series 1: each tranche expires 24 months after its vesting date. Series 3: exercisable from vest through a deadline defined in the report (forced automatic exercise if, within 48 months of allocation, intrinsic value equals or exceeds fair value). 2022 outline: each tranche expires 24 months after vesting (equivalently, maximum exercise periods of 36, 48 and 60 months from allocation — 2022 outline §§10.2 and 18.4). Additional expiration event (June 2026 report §2.3): if the average closing price over 30 trading days falls below a stated floor (NIS 40 in the 2025 press coverage of the June 2025 grant; confirm floor in the 2025 outline), unexercised options expire. Trading-prohibition periods can extend expiry by an equal number of days (2022 outline §10.2).
LUMI.TA.exercise_mechanism: Cashless / net exercise only. Offeree does not pay the exercise price; it is used only to compute the benefit. 2022 outline §10.4 formula for number of exercise shares: ((A × B) − (A × C)) / D, i.e. A×(B−C)/D, where A = options being exercised, B = Share Price for Benefit Calculation = the lower of (a) TASE closing price on the trading day preceding exercise and (b) the Ceiling Rate, C = exercise price, D = TASE closing price on the trading day preceding exercise. When the share is below the ceiling, B = D and the formula reduces to A×(B−C)/B. Ceiling Rate in the 2022 outline: first tranche 1.5× Base Price, second 1.6×, third 1.7×. June 2026 award ceiling ('Ceiling Price'): Series 1 first tranche 1.4× base price, second tranche 1.5×; Series 3 1.4×; Base Price = NIS 72.45 (30-day average), with dividend adjustment under §3.5. The June 2026 report points to Outline §10.6.2 for the cashless mechanism (full algebraic text of the 2025 outline was not retrieved).
LUMI.TA.rounding: No fractional shares. Any fraction below 0.5 is rounded down; 0.5 or higher is rounded up (2022 outline §10.4). A separate adjustment clause (§12.8) says the number of shares allocated after adjustments is rounded upward to the closest share — apply the specific net-exercise rounding in §10.4 when computing net shares.
LUMI.TA.tax_track: Israel Income Tax Ordinance Section 102, capital-gains track (מסלול רווח הון) with a trustee (2022 outline named IBI Capital Compensation and Trusts (2004) Ltd as trustee at publication). Plan filed with ITA 30 June 2022. June 2026 award is under the same 102 capital-gains track with trustee. Statutory 102 lock-up applies and may overlap vesting.
LUMI.TA.leaving_employer_rule: 2022 outline §11 (and June 2026 report incorporates the Option Plan's termination provisions): on ordinary termination (not death/disability), only already-vested/exercisable options may be exercised, and only for up to 180 days from termination (or earlier option expiry); unvested options expire. Dismissal without severance: all options, including vested unexercised, expire immediately. Death or disability: vested options exercisable until the earlier of original expiry and one year from termination, subject to Section 102. Transfer within the Bank group is not a termination. Board may expand entitlement.
LUMI.TA.notes_for_ui: The 12 June 2025 employee outline (MAGNA/Maya ref. 2025-01-042103) is the governing outline for 2025–2026 employee grants but was not found as a PDF on the English 2025 IR page and Maya/MAGNA HTML was blocked or incomplete in this run. Terms that the 11 June 2026 report expressly restates (30-day average strike, cashless exercise, Series 1/3 vesting, NIS 72.45, §102) are high confidence. The exact 2025-outline algebraic cashless formula (§10.6.2) was not read in the 2025 outline itself; the 2022 outline formula is cited for the 2022 plan mechanism, which the 2026 report says still applies as the Option Plan of 1 June 2022. Follow-up search on 26 Nov 2026 (Asia/Jerusalem): English Immediate Reports 2025 and 2026 pages were scraped; no 12.6.2025 outline PDF and no 28.4.2026 scribal-correction PDF appeared in the listings (April 2026 items were treasury-share and conference-call notices). The Hebrew path /he/about-leumi/Investor-Relations/Immediate-Reports-2025 and /he/Investor-Relations/Immediate-Reports returned 404. Web search for ref. 2025-01-042103 / 2026-01-039135 did not yield a hosted PDF. The 11.6.2026 award report remains the best public restatement of the 2025 outline terms.
LUMI.TA.public_default_note: Use the public 2022 outline / June 2026 award (30-trading-day average strike, 24 months after each vest in the public series-1 structure, §102, dividend reduces strike). Do not apply Aviad's private allocation letter (strike 69.2744, vest 1.6.2026/27/28, 36 months after each vest) as the bank-wide default; keep it as an employee-level override.

POLI.TA.plan_name: Option Plan submitted to ITA 4 March 2024; employee outline, material and immaterial private offering of restricted shares and options dated 8 April 2024 (ref. 2024-01-034483). Also a 2021 equity plan and a secondary plan for restricted shares / RSUs. Future awards under the 8 April 2024 outline of up to 3,400,000 options.
POLI.TA.strike_rule: For the 29 March 2026 grant: the higher of (1) the average price of the Bank share (adjusted for dividends and benefits) in the 30 trading days preceding the Board resolution (NIS 78.33) and (2) the closing price on the last trading day preceding that resolution (NIS 74.14) plus a 3% premium (NIS 76.36). Result: NIS 78.33. Not index-linked. The same 'higher of 30-day average vs. prior close + 3%' rule was used for the March 2025 additional-options award (exercise price NIS 51.71). The original April 2024 outline allocation used the 30-trading-day average (adjusted for dividends and benefits) and set NIS 33.89 for that grant. Future grants follow the outline / the award report then in force.
POLI.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: If a dividend (cash or in kind) record date falls after the Board allotment resolution and before exercise, the exercise price of unexercised options is reduced by the gross dividend per share (outline §2.5.5). The limit/cap price is also dividend-adjusted. Fair-value models therefore assume 0% dividend yield. Bonus shares and rights have separate adjustments.
POLI.TA.vesting_schedule: 29 March 2026 Additional Options (general case): three equal tranches — 1/3 exercisable from 1 January 2027, 1/3 from 1 January 2028, 1/3 from 1 January 2029 — subject to regulatory capital-adequacy conditions for the relevant vesting year (2026 / 2027 / 2028). Mid-year starts or upgrades may use unequal linear vesting. Bonus Options vest when awarded (no additional vesting period). April 2024 grant vesting was 1/3 from 1 Jan 2025, 1/3 from 1 Jan 2026, 1/3 from 1 Jan 2027, with capital-adequacy conditions. Restricted shares granted for a prior year are typically already earned and then locked up (36 months from the end of the year in respect of which they were granted, in the April 2024 CEO/managers grant).
POLI.TA.expiry_term: For the 29 March 2026 Additional Options, the award report states each tranche is exercisable until 31 December 2031, and §6.4 (amending the outline) says tranches expire when six years have elapsed from their vesting dates; Bonus Options expire 31 December 2031. The April 2024 outline had shorter windows (first tranche expire 4 years from vest; second and third 3 years from vest; e.g. first 2024 tranche exercisable 1 Jan 2025–31 Dec 2028). Use the award report that governs the specific grant.
POLI.TA.exercise_mechanism: Net exercise (cashless). April 2024 outline §1.3.8.4 formula: X = Y × (A − B) / A, where X = shares issued, Y = options exercised, A = TASE closing price on the last trading day preceding the exercise date, or — in the numerator only — the lower of that close and the Limit Price, B = exercise price. Offeree may in some cases elect ordinary (cash) exercise before the limit price is hit and after the 102 holding period (footnote 13). Forced automatic net exercise of a vested tranche if the close is at or above the Limit Price. Limit Price in the 2024 outline: 150% of exercise price. For the March 2026 grant the limit price of both Additional and Bonus Options is NIS 117.49 (dividend-adjusted). 2026 report says options are exercised using the net-exercise method in the outline; some later reports also note net exercise out of treasury/dormant shares held by the Bank.
POLI.TA.rounding: Any fraction of a share from the net-exercise calculation is rounded (up or down) to the closest whole share (outline §1.3.8.6). Same closest-whole-share rule for adjustment fractions (§2.5.4).
POLI.TA.tax_track: Section 102 capital-gains track with trustee (102(b)(3) cited in the outline). Option Plan submitted to ITA 4 March 2024. Bank also obtained ITA approvals for the net-exercise and adjustment mechanisms. Restricted shares under the same 102 capital-gains framework where applicable.
POLI.TA.leaving_employer_rule: Outline §2.6: restricted shares are generally not affected by termination. For options, unvested options expire on termination, with a possible pro-rata vest for the current tranche based on time employed in the relevant period. Dismissal in circumstances allowing denial of severance: all options, including vested, expire immediately. Options cannot be exercised after their stated expiration date. Transfer within the group is not a termination. Board may set different terms for a given offeree. Precise post-termination exercise window for already-vested options is in §§2.6.2–2.6.5 of the outline (not fully extracted in this run; consult the April 2024 outline PDF).
POLI.TA.notes_for_ui: Primary English convenience translations of Hebrew Magna reports; Hebrew original controls.

FIBI.TA.name_en: The First International Bank of Israel Ltd.
FIBI.TA.plan_name: Employee/officer option plan (ITA 'green track' ruling on net exercise dated 11 November 2025; equity plan tax filing cited as 4 February 2025 in related materials) and outline for an offering of securities to officers and other employees dated 28 April 2026.
FIBI.TA.strike_rule: Exercise price shall not fall below the higher of: (1) the average adjusted closing price of the Bank's share on TASE over the 30 trading days preceding Board approval of the allocation; and (2) the closing price on the last trading day preceding that Board approval. For the 28 April 2026 allocation the exercise price is NIS 253.25, subject to adjustments.
FIBI.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: If a cash dividend record date falls after grant and before actual exercise, the exercise price of unexercised options is reduced by the dividend per share, but not below the par value of the share (NIS 0.05). In-kind dividends, bonus shares and rights issues have separate adjustments (§2.4). The forced-exercise rate cap is also adjusted for subsequent dividends in the same way as the exercise price.
FIBI.TA.vesting_schedule: Unless the plan administrator sets otherwise, options vest one or two years from the allocation date, as determined by the plan administrator, subject to continued employment and performance targets: (i) total capital adequacy and CET1 ratios in the prior calendar year not below Banking Supervision minima; and (ii) return on equity of at least 8% in the prior year (if vesting is after one year) or average ROE of at least 8% over the two prior years (if vesting is after two years). Missed ROE can be re-tested on a deferred vesting date using a longer average. Specific 1-year vs 2-year split for the 135,258 options is to be set in allocation agreements (not itemized in the extracted outline text).
FIBI.TA.expiry_term: Exercisable from the vesting date until four years have elapsed from the allocation date. Outline itself may be used for new grants for 36 months from publication. Forced automatic net exercise if, after the 102 blocked period (whichever is later) and before expiry, the closing price reaches a rate cap of 75% above the closing price on the trading day preceding Board approval of the outline (for the current allocation: NIS 423.5), subject to the cap's dividend adjustment.
FIBI.TA.exercise_mechanism: Net exercise (cashless) based on the benefit component; the offeree does not pay the exercise price, which is used only to compute the benefit. The outline does not print an algebraic formula; the number of exercise shares 'shall be determined in accordance with the guidelines of the Tax Authority,' and the plan administrator may set implementation terms in the allocation agreement subject to Section 102 and ITA guidelines (ITA approved a green-track ruling on net exercise on 11 November 2025). If tax rules require, the Bank shall also allow an election to pay the exercise price in cash. Forced automatic net exercise at the rate cap as above.
FIBI.TA.rounding: No fractional shares on net exercise: fraction lower than 0.5 rounded down; 0.5 or higher rounded up (§2.3.5.5). Same nearest-whole-share rule (up or down) after adjustments (§2.4).
FIBI.TA.tax_track: Section 102 capital-gains track with a trustee (outline cites 102(b)(2) and 102(b)(3)). Grants that fail 102 conditions may be treated as 3(i) or 102(c).
FIBI.TA.leaving_employer_rule: Unless the allocation agreement says otherwise: on ordinary termination, only options already vested by the termination date may be exercised, and they remain exercisable until the original option end date (the end date is not pulled forward). Unvested options expire. Termination for cause (including circumstances with no severance, dishonesty, breach of fiduciary duty): all options, vested or not, expire with no consideration; the same if cause is found after termination and before exercise. Transfer within the Bank group is not a termination. Administrator may extend periods in exceptional cases, subject to ITA/102. Death/disability are addressed in the plan (see §2.7 remainder / §2.9). Clawback: if vesting was based on data later restated within three years after vest or exercise and no later than two years after leaving, unexercised options that would not have vested expire, and exercised benefit must be repaid within 60 days.
FIBI.TA.notes_for_ui: English IR convenience translation of the 28 April 2026 outline. Hebrew original on MAGNA/Maya controls. Algebraic net-exercise formula is deliberately not printed; implementers must not invent one.

DSCT.TA.plan_name: Employee stock-option outline exists; the Bank's English IR regulatory-filings archive lists 'Employee Stock Options (Non-Listed) Pursuant to an Outline' dated 29 January 2024. DSCT.TA.notes_for_ui: The outline exists and is catalogued as Magna ref. 2024-01-011079; this run could not open the file. Do not invent cashless or 30-day-average terms from other banks.

TEVA.TA.plan_name: Teva 2020 Long-Term Equity-Based Incentive Plan (shareholder-approved 11 June 2020, effective 1 July 2020; 68 million shares authorized). Prior 2015 Plan expired 30 June 2020 except for outstanding awards.
TEVA.TA.strike_rule: Not applicable to current RSU/PSU grants (no exercise price). Legacy outstanding options have stated exercise prices (e.g. a vested tranche in the $15.01–$20.00 range had a weighted-average exercise price of $18.97 as of 31 December 2025). The 10-K note does not restate the original strike-setting rule for those legacy options.
TEVA.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: Teva has not paid dividends on ordinary shares or ADSs since December 2017 (10-K note). No current dividend-adjustment practice for new options is described, and no options were granted in 2023–2025.
TEVA.TA.vesting_schedule: Outstanding options and RSUs generally vest between one and four years from grant date. PSUs generally vest three years from grant date. Continued-employment conditions are implicit in the unvested RSU/PSU tables (forfeitures are disclosed) but the 10-K note does not print a single mandatory cliff/graded calendar for all employees.
TEVA.TA.expiry_term: Contractual term of the (legacy) options is primarily ten years. RSUs/PSUs settle on vest (no option-style expiry).
TEVA.TA.exercise_mechanism: RSUs/PSUs convert into ordinary shares (or ADSs) on vesting, one share per unit as described in plan exhibits. Legacy options are conventional options (cash exercise implied by exercise-price tables); the 10-K note does not describe a mandatory net-exercise formula. Israeli employees' trustee/102 mechanics are not specified in this 10-K note.
TEVA.TA.tax_track: Not specified in the FY2025 Form 10-K stock-based compensation note. Israeli employees may be on Section 102, and US employees on standard RSU/option tax treatment, but that was not found in the pages read. Marked not found in this source.
TEVA.TA.leaving_employer_rule: Not specified in the 10-K note (see plan documents / award agreements; exhibit 10.23 is a plan-related exhibit in the SEC file). Unvested awards are forfeited in the ordinary course as shown by the forfeiture line, but post-termination vested-option windows were not extracted.
TEVA.TA.notes_for_ui: Primary source is Teva's Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2025, stock-based compensation note.

NVDA.plan_name: NVIDIA Corporation Amended and Restated 2007 Equity Incentive Plan; plus Amended and Restated 2012 Employee Stock Purchase Plan. Assumed awards from acquisitions are converted into NVIDIA RSUs.
NVDA.strike_rule: Not applicable to RSUs/PSUs (no strike). The 2007 Plan authorizes ISOs and non-statutory options, but the company states it grants RSUs, PSUs and market-based PSUs, not that it is currently granting options. ESPP purchase price = 85% of the lower of FMV on the offering-period commencement date and FMV on each purchase date.
NVDA.dividend_adjustment_rule: RSUs, PSUs and market-based PSUs are not eligible for cash dividends prior to vesting; grant-date fair values are discounted for dividend yield (about 0.03% in FY2026). No option dividend-adjustment rule is described because current grants are not options.
NVDA.vesting_schedule: Subject to certain exceptions, RSUs vest generally over four years, subject to continued service. PSUs vest over four years, subject to continued service and performance conditions. Market-based PSUs vest on approximately the third anniversary of grant, subject to market conditions. The Compensation Committee determines how many PSU and market-based PSU shares are eligible to vest based on pre-determined criteria. (A prior-year NVIDIA 10-K had described possible 25% then quarterly or quarterly-over-four-years RSU patterns; the FY2026 note states only 'generally over four years' and does not reprint that installment split.)
NVDA.expiry_term: RSUs/PSUs settle on vest (no option term). ESPP offering period is about 24 months, divided into four six-month purchase periods.
NVDA.exercise_mechanism: RSUs/PSUs convert into common stock on vesting. No cashless-option formula is described for current grants. ESPP is a discounted purchase of shares with withheld earnings (up to 25% of earnings, Board may decrease).
NVDA.tax_track: US employees: standard RSU/PSU ordinary-income taxation on vest (not specified in detail in this note). The 2007 Plan authorizes ISOs only for employees if options were used. Israeli or other local tracks are not described in this 10-K note.
NVDA.leaving_employer_rule: Vesting is subject to continued service. Forfeitures are estimated from historical forfeitures. Specific post-termination windows are in the plan/award agreements, not in this 10-K note.

AAPL.plan_name: Apple Inc. 2022 Employee Stock Plan (shareholder-approved 4 March 2022; maximum of approximately 1.3 billion shares authorized at approval). Employee Stock Purchase Plan, as amended 6 November 2024 (exhibit; terms not extracted from the 10-K note). Non-Employee Director Stock Plan is separate.
AAPL.strike_rule: Not applicable to RSUs. Grant-date fair value is based on the closing price of Apple common stock on the grant date. The 2022 Plan permits stock options and SARs, but the FY2026 10-K note describes RSU grants, not option grants.
AAPL.dividend_adjustment_rule: RSUs granted under the 2022 Plan have dividend equivalent rights, entitling holders to the same dividend value per share as common stockholders (so dividends are not applied by reducing a strike; they accrue as equivalents).
AAPL.vesting_schedule: RSUs granted under the 2022 Plan generally vest over four years, based on continued employment, and are settled upon vesting in common stock on a one-for-one basis. The 10-K does not specify whether vesting is annual, semi-annual or quarterly.
AAPL.expiry_term: RSUs settle on vest (no option expiry).
AAPL.exercise_mechanism: One-for-one share settlement on vest. The majority of RSUs that vested in 2026, 2025 and 2024 were net-share settled for taxes: Apple withheld shares equal to the employee's tax obligation and remitted cash to tax authorities ($6.9 billion in 2026). This is tax withholding, not an option net-exercise formula.
AAPL.tax_track: US employees: RSUs taxed as ordinary income on vest (standard); the 10-K describes net-share settlement for income and employment taxes. Local tracks (e.g. Israel 102) are not described in this note.
AAPL.leaving_employer_rule: Vesting is based on continued employment. Detailed post-termination rules are in the RSU award-agreement exhibits (forms of RSU agreement under the 2022 Plan are listed as exhibits), not in the 10-K narrative note.
AAPL.notes_for_ui: Form 10-K for the year ended 26 September 2026, filed 3 November 2026.

MSFT.plan_name: Company stock plans (including the 2017 Stock Plan, referenced in the 10-K) plus an Employee Stock Purchase Plan for all eligible employees, and an Executive Incentive Plan for executive officers and certain senior executives. The FY2026 10-K stock-plans note discusses 'stock awards' (RSUs and PSUs), not option grants.
MSFT.strike_rule: Not applicable to RSUs/PSUs. ESPP: employees may buy shares at three-month intervals at 90% of the fair market value on the last trading day of each three-month period, up to 15% of gross compensation during an offering period.
MSFT.dividend_adjustment_rule: Fair value of stock awards is based on the quoted price of common stock on the grant date less the present value of expected dividends not received during the vesting period (i.e. awards are discounted for missed dividends; not a strike reduction). Quarterly dividend assumptions used in FY2026 valuations were $0.83–$0.91 per share.
MSFT.vesting_schedule: Stock awards generally vest over a service period of four years or five years. Under the Executive Incentive Plan, RSUs generally vest ratably over four years; PSUs generally vest over a three-year performance period, with share count based on achievement of performance goals. Company-wide non-executive installment cadence beyond 'four or five years' is not further specified in this note.
MSFT.expiry_term: RSUs/PSUs settle as the award vests (no option term). ESPP purchases occur at three-month intervals.
MSFT.exercise_mechanism: Stock awards entitle the holder to receive Microsoft common stock as the award vests. The company issues new shares to satisfy vesting. No option net-exercise formula is described because this note does not report option grants. ESPP is a discounted purchase, not an option exercise.
MSFT.tax_track: US employees: standard RSU/PSU taxation (not detailed in this note). Local country tracks not described.
MSFT.leaving_employer_rule: Not specified in the FY2026 stock-plans note beyond ordinary forfeiture of unvested awards (10 million awards forfeited in FY2026). See plan/award agreements.
MSFT.notes_for_ui: Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended 30 June 2026, filed 29 July 2026.

MZTF.TA.plan_name: Employee offering outline dated 29 May 2024 (ref. 2024-01-054370), with option-warrant reserves for 2024, 2025 and 2026. First Lot issued 23 July 2024; Second Lot (2025) approved 23 March 2025.
MZTF.TA.strike_rule: For the 23 March 2025 Second Lot: ILS 171.5, equal to the average closing price over the 30 trading days preceding 23 March 2025, plus CPI linkage from the known index on the Board approval date until the known index on exercise, and subject to dividend adjustment (2025 allotment report §§2.3.1–2.3.2 and fair-value assumptions; 2024 Note 23 uses the same 'plus linkage differentials and dividend adjustment' formulation for the 2024 lot, whose strike was NIS 134). The prior trading day's close on 20 March 2025 was ILS 171.1. The May 2024 outline §2.20 governs adjustments. A November 2026 press discussion of a proposed 2027–2029 policy (CPI linkage optional, 6-year exercise) is not the 2025 grant.
MZTF.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: Exercise price is adjusted for dividends (2025 allotment report; 2024 Note 23 footnote to the NIS 134 strike: 'Plus linkage differentials and dividend adjustment'). The detailed formula is in Outline §2.20, not reprinted in the financial-statement note. Fair-value models used a 0% dividend yield because of this adjustment.
MZTF.TA.vesting_schedule: From Note 23 of the 2024 annual report (describing the 29 May 2024 plans, First Lot issued 23 July 2024): Plans A, B and C (officers and key employees) are in three equal lots exercisable from (1) two years after the issuance date, (2) 1 April 2027, and (3) 1 April 2028. Plans D and E (other managers, including those under collective agreements) vest as a single lot from the second anniversary of the issue date. Eligibility is contingent on the Bank's total capital-adequacy ratio and Tier I ratio for the award year not being below Bank of Israel minima, plus additional criteria in the outline (the 2025 allotment also refers to a benchmark-index condition in Outline §2.12). The 2025 Second Lot is stated to follow the same outline; its exact calendar is not reprinted in the 2025 allotment report beyond those outline references.
MZTF.TA.expiry_term: Plans A–C: each lot expires 18 months after its exercisability date (Note 23, 2024). Plans D and E: expire two years after the vesting date as defined in the Memorandum (Note 23, 2024). CEO 2024 options were exercisable as from 23 July 2026, with a closing-price cap of NIS 174 plus CPI (Note 23). The 2025 lot cap is 200% of the ILS 171.5 exercise price plus CPI (2025 allotment report). Valuation assumed expected lives of about 3.64–5.35 years (A–C) and 4.13 years (D–E).
MZTF.TA.exercise_mechanism: Net exercise / cashless: the 23 March 2025 allotment report states offerees (including the CEO) will not be required to pay the exercise price, which is used only to determine the benefit. There is a closing-rate cap (2025 lot: not more than 200% of the exercise price plus CPI, itself adjusted per Outline §2.20). The 2024 Note 23 describes a CEO cap of NIS 174 plus CPI for the 2024 lot but does not print the algebraic net-share formula; that remains in the 29 May 2024 outline. October 2026 exercises of 13,300 options into 2,531 shares are consistent with net settlement.
MZTF.TA.rounding: Not found in the 2024/2025 Note 23 or the 23 March 2025 allotment report. Search the 29 May 2024 outline (ref. 2024-01-054370).
MZTF.TA.tax_track: Section 102 capital-gains track (מסלול רווח הון). Explicitly stated in Note 23 of both the 2024 English annual report and the 2025 periodic report: options were allotted under the capital-gain track pursuant to Section 102; the benefit is taxed at the capital-gains rate on exercise; the Bank is not entitled to a tax deduction and (for the CEO) is not required to pay payroll tax on that benefit.
MZTF.TA.leaving_employer_rule: Not found in Note 23 or the 2025 allotment report. The 2024 Note 23 says details including reimbursement of the monetary benefit are in the 29 May 2024 outline.

PHOE.TA.plan_name: Option plan adopted 27 December 2018; filed with ITA on 3 January 2019 and 30 June 2024 (ITA also approved the net-exercise and adjustment mechanisms). Outline and immediate report dated 26 March 2026.
PHOE.TA.strike_rule: Prior-day TASE closing price plus a tranche-specific premium (§2.4.2). For this grant: first tranche NIS 182.60 (prior close + 10%); second tranche NIS 186.75 (prior close + 12.5%); third tranche NIS 190.90 (prior close + 15%). Future grants under the outline use the same method as of the relevant Board date unless the Board decides otherwise.
PHOE.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: If a cash-dividend record date falls after the Board allotment resolution and before exercise, the exercise price is reduced on the ex-dividend date by the gross dividend per share, but not below the TASE minimum share price (§2.10.7). Dividend does not change the number of exercise shares. Rights issues reduce the strike by the rights benefit component, not below par (§2.10.8). Bonus shares increase the share count as if the options had been exercised (§2.10.6).
PHOE.TA.vesting_schedule: Three equal tranches, subject to continued employment/engagement and performance conditions (§2.3): (1) 1/3 exercisable 26.3.2027–15.6.2028; (2) 1/3 exercisable 26.3.2028–15.6.2029; (3) 1/3 exercisable 26.3.2029–15.6.2030. Performance is cumulative: (a) a Board-set annual profit-per-share target (set by 31 March of the calendar year); 100% of a tranche requires at least 70% of that target, measured on FY2026 / FY2027 / FY2028 results respectively when the annual reports are published; (b) the insurance subsidiary's Solvency II economic solvency ratio must meet the regulator's circular over each of the three calendar years preceding the vest date (a shortfall cured within six months as allowed by the circular still counts). Missed profit targets may be re-tested in the following year until that tranche's expiry, but only if the solvency condition also holds in every relevant measurement year; a solvency miss in any measurement year causes immediate expiry of that tranche.
PHOE.TA.expiry_term: Each tranche expires at the end of its exercise window (15.6.2028 / 15.6.2029 / 15.6.2030) if unexercised, including vested options (§2.3.3, §2.9). Forced automatic net exercise if, after vest and after the 102 holding period and before expiry, the close is at or above the Limit Price: NIS 249.00 (first), NIS 261.45 (second), NIS 273.90 (third). Footnote 14 describes the caps as 40% / 45% / 50% above the respective tranche strikes; use the printed NIS caps for this grant. Automatic exercise waits until the 102 lock-up has ended.
PHOE.TA.exercise_mechanism: Net exercise (Cashless) is the default unless the Board provides otherwise (§2.8). Offeree does not pay the exercise price (used only to compute the benefit). Formula printed at §2.8.4: X = Y(A−B) / (C−Z), where X = shares issued, Y = vested, performance-met options being exercised, A = the lower of the TASE close on the last trading day before exercise and the Limit Price, B = adjusted exercise price (§2.4, subject to §2.10), C = that same prior-day close, Z = 0.00 (or, if par/minimum price must be paid because capitalization under Companies Law §302/304 is not available, NIS 1.00 par or the TASE minimum price of 30 agorot). Forced auto-exercise at the Limit Price uses the same net-exercise method.
PHOE.TA.rounding: No fractional shares; the number actually allotted is rounded to the nearest whole share (§2.8.4).
PHOE.TA.tax_track: Section 102(b)(3) capital-gains track with a trustee for employee offerees; Section 3(i) may apply as relevant. Plan filed with ITA 3 Jan 2019 and 30 June 2024. Statutory 102 lock-up can delay limit-price auto-exercise. If 102 conditions are not met, the 102 tax benefit may be lost (§2.12 area of the outline).
PHOE.TA.leaving_employer_rule: Default (§2.7.4): all options expire immediately on termination of employment/service; unvested options do not vest. Transfer within the group is not a termination. Exceptions (§2.7.5): (1) termination without 'cause' — already-vested options that have met performance conditions may be exercised within 90 days of termination or the end of the notice period (including payment in lieu), whichever is later, or 10 days after the end of the 102 lock-up, whichever is later; (2) death or disability — those vested/performance-met options, plus the tranche that would have vested at the end of the annual entitlement period in which death/disability occurred, may be exercised until the original expiry; (3) the Board may extend unexercised options, not beyond the original exercise period. Cause (§2.7.6): all options expire immediately at termination or when cause becomes known, whichever is earlier.

ICL.TA.plan_name: ICL Group Ltd. – Equity Compensation Plan (2024). Earlier outstanding awards remain under the amended 2014 Equity Compensation Plan. Terms below are from the 2024 Plan (Exhibit 4.2 to the 2024 20-F) and Note C of the FY2025 20-F share-based payments disclosure (R25).
ICL.TA.strike_rule: 2024 Plan §4.2: unless the Board states otherwise, the exercise price will not be less than the average closing price of the share on the Exchange in the 30 days preceding the Board’s allocation resolution. §4.3: unless the Board states otherwise, the exercise price is linked to the CPI (base = the index known on the Board approval date; adjusted by the ratio of the index known at exercise to the base). CPI linkage does not apply to offerees who are not Israeli tax residents and/or who are subject to U.S. tax laws. The FY2025 note confirms: 'The exercise price is linked to the known CPI as of the date of payment, which is the exercise date.'
ICL.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: 2024 Plan §13.4: unless the Board determines otherwise, on the ex-dividend date the exercise price of unexercised, unexpired options is reduced by the gross dividend per share in ILS, but not below par. This section does not apply to offerees who are not Israeli tax residents and/or who are subject to U.S. tax laws. The FY2025 note restates the same reduction on the ex-dividend date. Bonus shares and rights are adjusted under §§13.1–13.2.
ICL.TA.vesting_schedule: 2024 Plan §6.1: vesting times and any extra conditions are set in the grant letter, subject to continued employment/engagement. The FY2025 option table shows that grants from 8 February 2022 onward, including the 2024–January 2026 awards, vest in three equal tranches at the end of 12, 24 and 36 months after the grant date (2019-vintage awards used two equal tranches at 24 and 36 months).
ICL.TA.expiry_term: 2024 Plan §6.2 default: each vested portion is exercisable until 10 years after the Allocation Time (extended to the next business/trading day if that date is not one), unless the Board states otherwise; unexercised options then expire (§6.7). The FY2025 table prints explicit expiries for 2017–2018 grants (7 years after grant) and '5 years after the grant date' for 2019 grants. It does not print a contractual expiry date for the 2022–January 2026 grants; those are governed by the grant letter and, absent a contrary Board determination, the 10-year plan default. Black-Scholes expected lives for 2024/2025 grants (~3.0–3.5 years) are valuation assumptions, not the contractual term.
ICL.TA.exercise_mechanism: Default is Net Exercise (§4.6): the exercise price is not paid to the Company but is used to compute the shares issued. Formula as printed: number of shares = C × (A−B)/A, where A = fair value at exercise (listed-share prior-day closing price, §4.12), B = adjusted exercise price, C = options exercised. If the offeree must pay par or the TASE minimum (whichever is higher) because capitalization under Companies Law §304 is unavailable, the formula becomes C × (A−B)/(A−D), D = par or TASE minimum (§4.10). For §102 grants, net exercise is contingent on prior ITA approval if needed to preserve the tax benefit. The Board may instead require cash, check, shares, or a combination (§4.7/§4.11).
ICL.TA.rounding: No fractional shares; the number of shares is rounded to the closest whole share (§4.4, §4.8, §13.5).
ICL.TA.tax_track: Israeli employees: Section 102 capital-gains track with a trustee (2024 Plan §§3.3, 5.1; FY2025 note). Other offerees: §3(i) and/or §§2(1)/2(2), or the tax law of their country of residence.
ICL.TA.leaving_employer_rule: 2024 Plan §9. Ordinary termination (not death/disability, not 'no-severance' cause, and not a Board-elected rule-of-75 case): only options already vested may be exercised, for 90 days from termination (end of employment or end of notice/adjustment, whichever is later); unvested expire (§9.4, §9.8). Death or disability: vested options exercisable for 12 months, but not past the expiration time; the Board may accelerate unvested awards (§9.1). Circumstances in which the Company believes it may dismiss without severance (including criminal offences and breach of trust): all options, including vested, expire on the termination notice date (§9.2). At grant the Board may provide that if age + years of service ≥ 75, some or all unvested awards vest and are exercisable for 12 months (§9.3). Intra-group transfer is not a termination (§9.6).

ESLT.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: Plan §15.1 adjusts the number of underlying shares and the exercise price for bonus shares (share dividends), splits, combinations, recapitalizations and like events so as to preserve the proportionate equity portion and the total exercise price. The same section states that no adjustment is made by reason of a rights offering or other issuance of shares. The plan text does not provide for reducing the exercise price by a cash dividend. ESLT.TA.vesting_schedule: Subject to continued employment: 40% on the second anniversary of the Grant Date; 30% on the third anniversary; 30% on the fourth anniversary (§8.1). Unpaid leave postpones remaining vest dates and the expiry date by the number of unpaid-leave days (for U.S. taxpayers expiry still cannot fall after the 10th anniversary) (§8.2).

ESLT.TA.exercise_mechanism: Default is a Net-Exercise Mechanism (§10.1). Benefit = A × ((B−C)/B), and the shares issued equal Benefit / B, where A = vested options being exercised, B = Fair Market Value on the exercise date (TASE close on the prior trading day), C = exercise price of each option in NIS (USD strike converted at the Bank of Israel representative rate on the exercise date). Exercise is only on a TASE trading day and not on a record date or ex-date of a company event. Issuance is also subject to payment of nominal value and tax.
ESLT.TA.rounding: Any fraction of a share from the net-exercise calculation is rounded down to the nearest whole number (§10.3). Separately, §15.1 (capital adjustments) rounds 0.5 or more of a share up and less than 0.5 down.

Death or disability (or death during the 90-day window): vested options exercisable by the estate/assignees until the earlier of 12 months after death/disability or the Expiry Date (§13.2.1.2). Termination for Cause: all options, even vested, expire on the Termination Date (§13.2.2). Intra-group transfer is not a Termination.

Terms below for the broad employee/officer grant are from Note 25 of the 2025 periodic report (financial statements as of 31 December 2025).
MLSR.TA.strike_rule: For the 9 March 2025 employee/officer grant: NIS 326.85, subject to adjustments, being the higher of (1) the closing price on the last trading day before Board approval of the allocation and (2) the weighted-average closing price over a representative 30 trading days preceding that Board approval (Note 25.B). The CEO’s 2026 grant uses the same ‘higher of prior close and 30-trading-day average’ rule (there, NIS 427).
MLSR.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: Note 25 says the exercise price is ‘subject to adjustments’ but does not print the cash-dividend formula. See the 13 March 2023 outline / 10 March 2025 amendment and the 2013 plan.
MLSR.TA.vesting_schedule: Two lots of equal value: 101,485 options vest two years after the grant date; 84,955 vest three years after the grant date (Note 25.B).
MLSR.TA.expiry_term: Options are exercisable for two years from their vesting date (Note 25.B).
MLSR.TA.exercise_mechanism: Conversion into shares is by the net-exercise-in-shares method (מימוש נטו במניות / Cashless). The algebraic formula is not printed in Note 25.
MLSR.TA.tax_track: Section 102 capital-gains track with a trustee (Note 25.B, and the same wording for CEO awards in Note 25.A).
MLSR.TA.leaving_employer_rule: Not stated in Note 25. See the 2013 plan and the 2023/2025 outline.
MLSR.TA.notes_for_ui: High for strike rule, vest, expiry, 102 and cashless character, which the audited 2025 note restates; formula-level fields remain in the outline.

CAMT.TA.plan_name: 2018 Share Incentive Plan (and Sub-Plan for Grantees Subject to Israeli Taxation), adopted April 2018, replacing the 2014 Share Option Plan and the 2007 Restricted Share Unit Plan. The same 2018 umbrella is also described as including an RSU plan adopted in April 2018. Source: FY2025 20-F shareholders’-equity note (R23).
CAMT.TA.strike_rule: 2025 option grants: weighted-average exercise price $59.76 (the note does not state whether that is prior-day close, a 30-day average, or another rule). RSU ‘exercise price’ is determined by the Board in the grant notice, and unless the Board determines otherwise shall be no more than the underlying share’s nominal value; the Board may set it at $0.00.
CAMT.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: Option valuation assumptions for 2024 and 2025 show a dividend yield of '—'. No cash-dividend adjustment to the option strike is stated in R23.
CAMT.TA.vesting_schedule: For the 2025 option grants, the valuation table lists a vesting period of 1.0 year (and unrecognized option cost at year-end is to be recognized over one year). A prefatory sentence in the same note still refers to recognition ‘over the vesting period of four years’ as a general option-model description; the 2025 grant-specific figure is 1.0 year. RSU vesting schedules are determined by the Board in the grant notice and are not tabulated; unrecognized RSU expense of $26,088 thousand will be recognized in the years 2026 to 2029, which is consistent with multi-year vest.
CAMT.TA.expiry_term: The contractual life of the stock options is 7 years. RSUs ‘become automatically exercised’ on vest.
CAMT.TA.exercise_mechanism: Options: standard exercise at the strike. RSUs vest and automatically exercise into shares, typically at par or $0. No option net-exercise formula is described. An Israeli sub-plan exists; its cashless mechanics, if any, are not in R23.
CAMT.TA.tax_track: There is a Sub-Plan for Grantees Subject to Israeli Taxation. R23 does not state whether the company has elected the Section 102 capital-gains route. U.S. tax treatment is not detailed.
CAMT.TA.leaving_employer_rule: Forfeited RSUs return to the pool (17,927 RSUs forfeited in 2025). Detailed post-termination windows are not in R23.
CAMT.TA.notes_for_ui: High for current instruments, 2025 volumes, option contractual life and RSU par/$0 settlement; employee vest cadence for RSUs remains Board-determined.

NVMI.TA.plan_name: Share Incentive Plan adopted by the Board on 1 August 2017 (maximum 2,500,000 ordinary shares, subject to future increases or decreases). Compensation Policy for Executive Officers and Directors adopted by shareholders on 18 June 2025. Source: FY2025 20-F (zk2634307.htm), including Item 6 and the share-based compensation / RSU tables.
NVMI.TA.strike_rule: Not applicable to current RSU grants (fair value is the market value of the underlying share on the grant date). For any options, ‘in accordance with our current equity-based compensation policy, the exercise price of granted options is equal to the closing sale price of the Company's ordinary shares on Nasdaq on the day of grant.’ Legacy options outstanding at year-end 2025 have strikes in the $22.56–$102.35 range.
NVMI.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: The company ‘has historically not paid dividends and has no foreseeable plans to pay dividends.’ No option-strike dividend adjustment is described.
NVMI.TA.vesting_schedule: RSUs: expense is recognized over the requisite service period using the accelerated method; the note does not specify the employee installment cadence. Compensation policy default for executive officers (other than directors): gradual vesting over three to five years, unless a specific award agreement approved by the compensation committee and the Board provides otherwise. CEO awards described in the 20-F (time-based and performance RSUs for Mr. Waisman) vest over four years in four equal annual installments, with performance conditions on revenue budget and/or non-GAAP operating profit and a four-year average ROE catch-up. Those CEO conditions should not be treated as the default for all employees.
NVMI.TA.expiry_term: RSUs settle on vest. No new option contractual term applies to 2023–2025 grants. The Board, after compensation-committee approval, may extend the period for which an award remains exercisable.
NVMI.TA.exercise_mechanism: RSU settlement into ordinary shares on vest. Legacy options, if exercised, are at the grant-date Nasdaq close strike. No net-exercise formula is stated for current awards.
NVMI.TA.rounding: Not stated in the FY2025 20-F sections reviewed.
NVMI.TA.tax_track: Not described in the FY2025 20-F sections reviewed (no Section 102 election wording was found in those passages). Do not assume a track until a plan addendum is read.
NVMI.TA.leaving_employer_rule: 21,219 RSUs were canceled in 2025. Detailed post-termination rules are in the 2017 plan, not extracted from the 20-F note.
NVMI.TA.notes_for_ui: Current grants are RSUs only; leftover options are fully vested.

BEZQ.TA.name_en: Bezeq The Israel Telecommunication Corp. Ltd.
BEZQ.TA.plan_name: Employee offering outline published concurrently with the 13 November 2026 special-general-meeting notice (the outline PDF itself was not retrieved). The 13 November 2026 meeting notice (primary) describes chair and CEO grants under that outline and restates the company’s compensation-policy strike rule. Compensation policy approved by shareholders on 25 January 2026 (ref. 2026-01-008101).
BEZQ.TA.strike_rule: Compensation policy (restated in the 13 November 2026 notice §§2.1.2): the exercise price used to compute the benefit shall not be less than the higher of (a) the average TASE closing price over the 30 trading days preceding Board (or duly authorized committee) approval of the grant and (b) the TASE close on the last trading day before that approval. For this grant the prior close was NIS 6.87. The first award’s strike is NIS 7.11, equal to that 30-trading-day average; the second award’s strike is NIS 7.82. Each grant is split into two equal awards with different strikes and different ‘target prices’ (מחיר יעד / תנאי מחיר למימוש): NIS 8.00 and NIS 9.00. The target-price condition is satisfied if the average close over at least 30 consecutive trading days, measured at a check date from 30 trading days before vest through expiry (but before actual exercise), is at least the target; it need not hold on the exercise date itself. Strikes are subject to outline §2.5.6 adjustments. Option-fraction rounding may change the number in each award (footnote 3).
BEZQ.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: The notice states that customary adjustments apply, including on a dividend distribution, as set out in the outline, and the valuation tables expressly mark ‘adjustment of the exercise price for a dividend distribution — yes’. The valuation assumed a dividend yield of zero because of that adjustment. The algebraic adjustment is in outline §2.5.6, not printed in the notice.
BEZQ.TA.vesting_schedule: Three equal annual tranches. The first vests on 10 November 2027 (one year after the allocation date); each later tranche vests one year after the prior tranche, subject to the other vesting conditions in the outline, including the target-price condition described above.
BEZQ.TA.expiry_term: Each tranche expires 18 months after it vests, i.e. 30, 42 and 54 months from the allocation date.
BEZQ.TA.exercise_mechanism: Net exercise, subject to an appropriate ITA tax ruling: the exercise price is not paid in cash to the company but is used to compute the number of shares actually delivered, ‘as detailed in the outline’. The algebraic formula is not printed in the meeting notice. Valuation also assumes expected early exercise of 2–4 (a model input, not a plan cap).
BEZQ.TA.rounding: Footnote 3: the number of options in each award may change depending on rounding of option fractions. Share-rounding on net exercise is in the outline, not in the notice.
BEZQ.TA.tax_track: Not stated in the 13 November 2026 meeting notice (no Section 102 wording). See the outline.
BEZQ.TA.leaving_employer_rule: The notice says the outline’s other provisions apply, including termination of employment and a sale event. Those sections were not read.
BEZQ.TA.notes_for_ui: High for strike rule, hurdles, vest, expiry, cashless character and the existence of a dividend adjustment, all restated in a primary meeting notice. Formula, 102 and leave still require the outline.

BIG.TA.plan_name: Employee option plan adopted by the Board in November 2016, as amended from time to time. Each employee/officer grant described in Note 19 of the 2024 annual financial statements was made under that plan. Source: 2024 periodic report (financial statements as of 31 December 2024) Note 19, and events note in the Q1 2026 interim financial statements (approved 25 May 2026).
BIG.TA.strike_rule: Note 19 (2024): the exercise price is set by reference to the TASE closing price on the eve of Board approval or the average share price over the 30 trading days preceding the Board date. The note does not say ‘the higher of’ the two; the wording is disjunctive. The price is subject to adjustments as set out in the plan. The 29 January 2026 grant was valued at an exercise price of NIS 758.
BIG.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: Note 19 says the exercise price is subject to adjustments as detailed in the plan terms. The cash-dividend formula is not printed in Note 19 or the Q1 2026 events note.
BIG.TA.vesting_schedule: Under the November 2016 plan as restated in Note 19: one-third becomes exercisable two years after the allocation date; one-third after three years; one-third after four years. The Q1 2026 note does not state a different schedule for the January 2026 grant, and describes that grant as an employee/officer award under the company’s plan.
BIG.TA.expiry_term: Plan default as restated in Note 19: the first tranche is exercisable from year 2 through year 5 after allocation; the second from year 3 through year 5; the third from year 4 through year 5. All unexercised options therefore expire five years after the allocation date, unless a specific grant provides otherwise (not stated for January 2026).
BIG.TA.exercise_mechanism: Net exercise: at exercise the offeree may elect not to pay the exercise price, and is issued only the number of shares that reflects the cash benefit embedded in the options (Note 19). The algebraic formula is not printed.
BIG.TA.rounding: Not stated in Note 19 or the Q1 2026 events note.
BIG.TA.tax_track: Not stated in Note 19 or the Q1 2026 events note (no Section 102 wording on the pages reviewed). See the 2016 plan / any outline for a given grant.
BIG.TA.leaving_employer_rule: Not stated in Note 19 (the 2022 valuation used a 4.1% departure rate; the 2026 grant used 12% / 6.08%, which are valuation assumptions, not leave windows).
BIG.TA.notes_for_ui: High for vest/expiry, cashless character, the January 2026 grant size and NIS 758 strike, all from audited or reviewed financial-statement notes. Do not use press figures (e.g. 462,000 options / 97 employees) that conflict with the 586,250 figure in the Q1 2026 note.

ORA.TA.plan_name: 2018 Incentive Compensation Plan, amended and restated in June 2022 and again in May 2024 (share-reserve increases and a one-year mandatory minimum vesting period). Source: Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2025, stock-based compensation / 2018 plan note.
ORA.TA.strike_rule: Not applicable to current RSU/PSU grants. The plan still authorizes incentive stock options and SARs. Upon exercise, SARs deliver shares equal to the increase in value of the award between the grant date and the exercise date. Legacy options/SARs remain outstanding (101,000 exercisable at year-end 2025; weighted-average exercise price of exercisable awards $70.26).
ORA.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: The plan may provide dividend equivalents. Valuation of 2025 awards used a 0.69% dividend yield (2024: 0.73%). The 10-K note does not state whether unvested RSUs accrue dividend equivalents.
ORA.TA.vesting_schedule: Typical employee SAR/RSU/PSU vesting under the plan: either (a) 50% on the second anniversary and 25% on each of the third and fourth, or (b) 33.3% on each of the first, second and third anniversaries. Director awards typically vest 100% on the first anniversary. The March 2025 employee/management RSUs and PSUs have vesting periods of between 1 and 3 years. PSUs are paid out based on three-year relative TSR versus the S&P 500 or on three-year megawatt COD capacity targets. A June 2022 amendment imposed a one-year mandatory minimum vesting period.
ORA.TA.expiry_term: The term of stock-based awards typically ranges from six to ten years from the grant date. RSUs/PSUs settle on vest. Legacy options/SARs remain subject to that contractual range.
ORA.TA.exercise_mechanism: RSUs: a right to receive one share of common stock once vesting conditions are met. PSUs settle in shares based on performance. SARs settle in shares for the appreciation. No option net-exercise formula is described for current grants.
ORA.TA.rounding: Not stated in the FY2025 10-K note.
ORA.TA.tax_track: U.S.: RSUs/PSUs standard ordinary-income taxation on vest (not spelled out beyond award mechanics). The plan authorizes ISOs. Israeli employees and any Section 102 election are not described in this note.
ORA.TA.leaving_employer_rule: 25,000 awards were forfeited in 2025. Detailed post-termination windows are not in the FY2025 plan note.
ORA.TA.notes_for_ui: Current disclosed grants are RSUs and PSUs; options/SARs are legacy.

CYBR.TA.name_en: Palo Alto Networks, Inc. (successor to CyberArk Software Ltd.)
CYBR.TA.plan_name: Palo Alto Networks 2021 Equity Incentive Plan (effective December 2021, replacing the 2012 Plan) and the 2012 Employee Stock Purchase Plan (amended 29 August 2017). CyberArk awards were assumed in the acquisition and retain their original terms, settled in PANW common stock; no new awards are granted under assumed plans. Source: PANW Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended 31 July 2026 (filed under CIK 0001327567).
CYBR.TA.strike_rule: Not applicable to current RSU/PSU grants. The 2021 Plan authorizes stock options, SARs, RSAs, RSUs, PSAs, PSUs and PSOs, but the FY2026 activity tables show RSU/PSU grants and only residual PSO exercises (none left outstanding). ESPP purchase price: 85% of the lower of FMV on the first trading day of the offering period or on the purchase date.
CYBR.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: Unvested RSUs ‘do not have the voting and dividend participation rights of common stock’ until they vest. No option-strike dividend adjustment is relevant to current grants.
CYBR.TA.vesting_schedule: The majority of equity awards are RSUs, which generally vest over four years from the grant date. PSUs generally vest over one to four years; the number that vest depends on performance and/or market conditions. FY2026/FY2025 PSUs with service, performance and market conditions: service over one to three years; performance based on an average of next-generation security annualized recurring revenue and non-GAAP net income per diluted share. Older FY2023 market-condition PSUs (stock-price hurdles of $116.67–$166.67 on a 30-trading-day average) had all price targets met by 31 July 2026, with remaining service conditions still to be satisfied. Assumed CyberArk awards retain the time-based vesting in their original agreements.
CYBR.TA.expiry_term: RSUs/PSUs settle on vest. PSOs outstanding at the start of FY2026 were fully exercised during the year (none remain). ESPP: each 24-month offering period has four consecutive 6-month purchase periods, with purchase dates on the first trading day on or after 28 February and 31 August.
CYBR.TA.exercise_mechanism: RSU/PSU settlement in PANW common stock on vest. ESPP: payroll deductions of up to 15% of eligible compensation, subject to 3,750 shares per six-month purchase period and $25,000 of stock per calendar year. If FMV on the purchase date is lower than on the first day of the offering period, the current offering is cancelled after purchase and a new 24-month offering begins. 2 million ESPP shares were purchased in each of FY2024–FY2026 (FY2026 average purchase price $133.39). 47 million ESPP shares remained available at 31 July 2026.
CYBR.TA.rounding: Not stated in the FY2026 10-K plan note.
CYBR.TA.tax_track: U.S. RSU/PSU ordinary-income taxation on vest and ESPP tax rules are not spelled out beyond withholding (the PSO table notes shares withheld to satisfy exercise price and tax). Local tracks including Israel 102 for former CyberArk employees are not described in this 10-K note.
CYBR.TA.leaving_employer_rule: Forfeitures are shown in the RSU/PSU table (2 million RSUs and 2 million PSUs forfeited in FY2026). Detailed post-termination windows are in the 2021 Plan / award agreements and, for assumed CyberArk awards, in the original CyberArk terms. No additional awards are granted under assumed plans; forfeited assumed awards are not returned to those plans.
CYBR.TA.notes_for_ui: If the calculator also has a PANW S&P 100 ticker, this is the same plan.

ENLT.TA.plan_name: The company’s current options plan (used for both options and RSUs/PSUs). Terms below are the general rules in Note 18 of the FY2025 20-F financial statements, plus the material 2025 allocations described there. A historical 2010 employee option plan is referred to elsewhere in the 20-F; current grants are described as being under the current options plan.
ENLT.TA.strike_rule: Note 18 states a specific USD exercise price for each material option grant (for example USD 24.62 on 4 August 2025 and USD 25.59 on 1 October 2025) but does not print a general pricing formula (such as a 30-day average or prior close). The general description refers only to cashless exercise ‘as specified in the options plan’. The plan document itself was not retrieved.
ENLT.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: Options are subject to standard adjustments under the options plan, including in the event of a dividend distribution and of a rights issue or bonus shares. The algebraic adjustment is not printed in Note 18.
ENLT.TA.vesting_schedule: Default option vesting in Note 18, unless a grant provides otherwise: 50% at 24 months after grant, 25% at 36 months, 25% at 48 months. The 4 August 2025 and 1 October 2025 option grants instead vest 25% annually over four years from the grant date. RSUs generally vest 25% on each anniversary of the grant date over four years (external-director RSUs granted 17 April 2024 vest equally over three years). PSUs were also granted on 1 October 2025; their performance metrics are not fully extracted from the following paragraph of the note.
ENLT.TA.expiry_term: Not stated as a general contractual term in the Note 18 general description (the note tracks expirations in the movement table: 127,174 options expired in 2025). See the options plan and award agreements.
ENLT.TA.exercise_mechanism: Options are exercised under a cashless mechanism ‘as specified in the options plan’. The algebraic formula is not printed in Note 18. RSUs entitle the offeree to ordinary NIS 0.1 shares on the vesting dates.
ENLT.TA.tax_track: Not stated in the Note 18 pages reviewed (no Section 102 wording there). Do not assume a track until the plan or an Israeli addendum is read.
ENLT.TA.leaving_employer_rule: Options: on termination of employment the offeree is given a limited period to exercise vested options only; the length of that period is not stated in Note 18. In terminations defined as ‘severe’, the company may revoke rights. RSUs: vested RSUs remain with the offeree; unvested RSUs are forfeited.
ENLT.TA.notes_for_ui: High for default and 2025 vest schedules, cashless character, dividend-adjustment existence and 2025 grant volumes, all from the audited 20-F note.

ELAL.TA.plan_name: 2022 equity plan, plus an employee offering outline approved by the Board for up to 10,000,000 unlisted, non-transferable options (the ‘employee outline plan’), grants being made under and subject to the 2022 plan. Source: Note 18 of the 2025 consolidated financial statements (published on the IR site; report date 24 February 2026).
ELAL.TA.strike_rule: Note 18 footnotes: for grants under the employee outline, the exercise price is the average share price on the TASE over the 30 trading days preceding the Board’s grant decision, and is not linked to any index. For an allocation to a company officer, which is subject to the compensation policy, the exercise price is the higher of that 30-trading-day average and the TASE close on the last trading day before the Board decision. Examples: April 2024 outline grants used NIS 4.80; November 2024 grants NIS 7.55; the 5 January 2026 outline grant to nine employees used NIS 15.23 (table). These listed prices are before the 27 January 2026 dividend adjustment.
ELAL.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: The 2022 plan adjusts the exercise price for dividends. Note 18 states that the strikes in the tables are before adjustment for a dividend of NIS 0.57 per share on 27 January 2026, after the balance-sheet date, ‘in accordance with and subject to the 2022 plan’.
ELAL.TA.vesting_schedule: Employee-outline default, subject to continuous service: one-third becomes exercisable after each 12 complete months, over three years, from a grant-specific start date (1 April 2024 for the original 46-employee grant; 19 November 2024 for the three-employee grant; 5 January 2026 for the nine-employee grant). Officer awards have used 3-year, 3.5-year or 4.5-year three-tranche calendars (for example 30 June 2026/2027/2028). Restricted shares follow the same vest calendar as the options in the same grant.
ELAL.TA.expiry_term: Employee-outline options: exercisable from vest until 7 years from the grant date (the 5 January 2026 employee grant is instead exercisable until 3.5 years from grant). Unexercised options expire at the end of that window and confer no further rights. Some officer grants have used 4- or 5-year windows from grant.
ELAL.TA.exercise_mechanism: Options and restricted shares are granted for no cash consideration (ללא תמורה). Note 18 does not describe a net-exercise / cashless formula for paying the strike; do not infer one. Restricted shares are company ordinary shares subject to restriction until vest.
ELAL.TA.tax_track: Section 102 capital-gains track with a trustee, expressly stated for the employee-outline grants and for the officer grants described in Note 18.
ELAL.TA.leaving_employer_rule: Not fully stated. Footnotes record that options of offerees who left before vest were deducted from the outstanding counts, and that 363,152 restricted shares became dormant treasury shares when offerees left before vest. Post-termination exercise windows for already-vested awards are not printed in this note.
ELAL.TA.notes_for_ui: High for 102, strike rule (including the officer ‘higher of’ test), vest, expiry, dividend adjustment and the 5 January 2026 employee grant, all from the audited 2025 financial statements.

OPCE.TA.plan_name: July 2017 Option Plan for offerees, revised in May 2018 to allow RSUs and to amend the change-of-control adjustment. Source: Note 16 of the FY2025 consolidated financial statements (English convenience translation of the official Hebrew annual report published 12 March 2026). The Hebrew annual report controls.
OPCE.TA.strike_rule: Each option’s exercise price is determined per offeree and will be at least the average share price in the 30 trading days prior to the Board’s allocation decision, unlinked, and subject to the adjustments in the plan. Examples in the 2025–2026 table: NIS 31.98 (March 2025 executives), NIS 43.39 (July 2025 CEO), NIS 94.67 (March 2026 officer).
OPCE.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: The exercise price is subject to certain adjustments set out in the Options Plan, including in respect of a dividend distribution and an issuance of rights. The algebraic adjustment is not printed in Note 16. RSUs confer a dividend-equivalent amount if the company distributes a dividend, but no voting or other shareholder rights before conversion into shares.
OPCE.TA.vesting_schedule: Options and RSUs are allocated in three or four equal tranches: tranche 1 vests 12 months from grant; tranche 2 at 24 months; tranche 3 at 36 months; tranche 4 (if used) at 48 months.
OPCE.TA.expiry_term: Tranche 1 expires 36 months after its vesting date. Tranches 2, 3 and 4 each expire 24 months after their respective vesting dates.
OPCE.TA.exercise_mechanism: The offered securities ‘are exercisable at net’. The algebraic cashless formula is not printed in Note 16. Each option is exercisable for one ordinary NIS 0.01 share. Each RSU converts into one such share for no consideration.
OPCE.TA.tax_track: Section 102 capital-gains track with a trustee, expressly stated for the allocated options (and for options and RSUs allocated from time to time in an equity track with a trustee).
OPCE.TA.leaving_employer_rule: Not fully stated. Note 16 records that options expired in 2025, 2024 and 2023 inter alia following exits of company employees. The post-termination window for already-vested awards is not printed. Options are non-transferable except to successors on death, as set out in the plan.
OPCE.TA.notes_for_ui: English convenience translation of the official Hebrew FS; the Hebrew annual report is controlling. High for strike floor, vest/expiry calendar, 102, dividend-adjustment existence and 2025–2026 grant table.

STRS.TA.plan_name: Employee compensation plan of May 2003, last updated May 2023 (the ‘Plan’), under which the company grants warrants/options to group employees. Source: Note 20 of the FY2025 consolidated financial statements.
STRS.TA.strike_rule: For grants from 12 September 2016, the Board (or its committees) chooses one of three alternatives: (1) the average closing price over the 30 trading days preceding the grant date, plus a premium set by the Board/committees; (2) the same 30-trading-day average with no premium, CPI-linked; or (3) the same 30-trading-day average with no premium and no CPI linkage. The 2025 manager grants have strikes a few shekels above the contemporaneous share price (e.g. 74.82 vs 71.12; 89.00 vs 87.37; 95.65 vs 92.96), consistent with alternative (1), but the note does not label which alternative was used for those grants.
STRS.TA.dividend_adjustment_rule: The exercise price or the conversion ratio of each warrant is adjusted proportionally for the benefit arising from a bonus-share issue (or any other increase or decrease in the number of ordinary shares for which the company received no consideration), a consolidation or redivision of shares, a rights issue, or a dividend. Note 23.3 confirms that dividends paid in 2024–2025 led to an adjustment of the employees’ exercise prices, by reference to Note 20.1.1.
STRS.TA.vesting_schedule: Default for grants from 20 March 2016: 50% exercisable from two years after the determining date and 50% from three years after that date. Exception: the 23 October 2025 grant vests 80% after two years and 20% after three years.
STRS.TA.expiry_term: A general contractual expiry (for example a fixed number of years from grant) is not printed in the Note 20 paragraphs reviewed. Valuation ‘expected lives’ for the 2025 grants were 3.65–4.65 years (January and May) and 2.41–3.41 years (October). See the plan and award agreements for the contractual term.
STRS.TA.exercise_mechanism: Net exercise in shares, without payment of the strike: the offeree is allotted a number of shares reflecting the embedded benefit, equal to the difference between (i) a minimum exercise-share price set by the employee if the employee set one, or otherwise the last closing price of an ordinary share on the trading day before exercise, and (ii) the strike, multiplied by the number of warrants exercised. Because the offeree must still pay par value on the shares issued, additional shares are allotted to cover that par-value payment.
STRS.TA.tax_track: The plan was approved under Section 102 of the Income Tax Ordinance; the warrants are deposited with a trustee. Employees bear any tax imposed on the plans.
STRS.TA.leaving_employer_rule: If employment ends other than for ‘cause’ as defined in the plan and the employment agreement, and the employee has more than two years’ tenure in the group, the company may (with Board/committee approval) extend the exercise window by a further 180 days beyond the ordinary 180 days from termination, so that the offeree may exercise for 360 days, and may provide for early vesting of warrants that would have vested within six months of termination. On death, disability or legal incapacity, the employee or heirs may exercise all warrants allocated to the employee, in accordance with the original vesting and expiry dates.
STRS.TA.notes_for_ui: High for net-exercise mechanics (including the employee-set minimum and par-value top-up shares), the three strike alternatives, default and October 2025 vest schedules, 102, dividend adjustment, and leave.

NVPT.TA.plan_name: 2018 equity compensation plan, adopted by the General Partner’s board on the basis of an outline first approved by the meeting of participation-unit holders on 18 July 2018, for officers, employees and service providers who are not controlling shareholders. Awards are options and RSUs over the Partnership’s participation units. Source: Note 15 (and officer-specific Note 18C) of the FY2025 consolidated financial statements.
NVPT.TA.strike_rule: Plan default for options (Note 15A): the exercise price is based on a weighted average of the closing prices of the participation units over the 30 trading days preceding the effective date, plus a premium of 10%–30% according to the vesting period of each tranche. Officer grants have used stated NIS prices per tranche (for example 132.39 / 137.68 for the November 2025 award) and must not be treated as the employee default.

Plan default for RSUs: three tranches once two cumulative conditions are met — (a) employment duration of 18–42 months from the effective date, and (b) a target price equal to the 30-trading-day weighted average closing price at the effective date plus a 10%–30% premium.
